summary: Submission approvable with 2 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Misattributed citation: two claims cited to CBS News are not present in the CBS News snapshot
findings.details: In the 4th 'What We Know' bullet, the 'prospective only' / does-not-affect-already-purchased-devices claim is jointly cited to CBS News and Robotics and Automation News. In the 5th bullet, the federal-government-purchase-exemption claim is cited to CBS News alone. The CBS News snapshot (source-7.html.gz, an AP/CBS wire story on the market/trade angle) contains zero occurrences of 'federal government', 'prospective', 'previously', 'already purchased', 'exempt', or 'carve' — it does not discuss the Covered List's prospective-only design or the federal-government carve-out at all. Both claims ARE accurately reported, but only by Robotics and Automation News (source-6.html.gz: 'does not impact a consumer's continued use of devices they previously acquired'; 'does not impact purchase or use by the federal government at all'), not by CBS. The 4th bullet's dual citation survives on the R&A half; the 5th bullet's sole CBS citation does not survive review as written.

content_preview.title: FCC Bans New Chinese-Made Humanoid Robots and Robot Dogs, Citing National Security Risks
content_preview.summary: The FCC added foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots to its Covered List, blocking new imports as China holds roughly 85% of the global market.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Federal Communications Commission has added foreign-made "advanced robotic devices" — humanoid robots and four-legged quadrupeds, along with connected power inverters — to its Covered List, blocking new imports of the equipment on national security grounds. The order, [DA 26-786](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-786A1.txt), was released July 28, 2026, one day after the Executive Branch national security determinations that triggered it were issued on July 27, 2026, ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure), 795 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, non-sensational tone throughout; no AI self-reference. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags the undisclosed technical definition of 'advanced robotic devices' and the unknown Conditional Approval application volume, which is honest hedging rather than filler.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 8 cited sources. 7 of 8 snapshots were fetched and saved to sources/2026-07/fcc-bans-new-chinese-made-humanoid-robots-and-robot-dogs-citing-national-security-risks/ (source-0 through source-3, source-5 through source-7); I decompressed each with gunzip, re-hashed the plaintext, and confirmed every sha256 matches the manifest exactly. techxplore.com (would-be source-4) failed with HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) and has no snapshot file; as a last resort I used a live WebFetch of the URL, which confirmed the 85% China market-share figure, the ~15,000-units-in-2025/Unitree+AGIBOT-5,000-each figures, and the Kangyuxiao Li Morningstar quote are all present on the live page verbatim/near-verbatim — noting explicitly this was a live fetch, not the archived snapshot the provenance chain records. docs.fcc.gov (source-0, the primary FCC order DA 26-786) was read in full: confirms the order was released July 28, 2026, the two National Security Determinations were sent to the FCC on July 27, 2026, the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019 / 47 U.S.C. §§ 1601-1609 citation, and both block quotes attributed to 'the FCC order' verbatim ('collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors...' and 'networked capabilities of advanced robotic systems create extensive vulnerabilities...'). tech.yahoo.com (source-1) and abcnews.com (source-2) independently confirm the same two block quotes verbatim. abcnews.com (source-2) confirms: 85% market share, ~15,000 units shipped globally in 2025 with Unitree/AGIBOT each shipping 5,000+ and Tesla/Figure AI 'a few hundred or less,' the Brendan Carr 'secure America's critical supply chains' quote, the Mao Ning quote verbatim, the Kangyuxiao Li quote verbatim, and the September 2026 Trump-Xi meeting. fortune.com (source-3) is the same AP wire story as ABC News/CBS News (bylined Associated Press + Chan Ho-Him) and corroborates the same figures and quotes, plus the Morgan Stanley $15B-by-2030 forecast cited to it. techcrunch.com (source-5) confirms the 'exceptions may be granted if a device poses no risk' characterization and that existing power-inverter devices are unaffected. roboticsandautomationnews.com (source-6) is the most detailed trade-press account and confirms the Brendan Carr 'I welcome these Executive Branch national security determinations...' quote verbatim, the Conditional Approval process (DoW for robots; DoW or DHS for power inverters), the prospective-only design, and explicitly states the update 'does not affect sales to, or use by, the federal government or federal agencies.' cbsnews.com (source-7) is again the same AP wire story as ABC/Fortune and independently confirms the market-share, units-shipped, and quote claims cited to ABC News — but does NOT contain any language about the prospective-only design, previously-purchased-device carve-out, or federal-government exemption (verified by keyword grep for 'federal government', 'prospective', 'previously', 'already purchased', 'exempt', 'carve' — zero hits). See the misattribution finding below.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All directly-quoted material is verbatim and correctly attributed to a source that actually contains it. All checked numeric specifics (85% market share, ~15,000 units globally in 2025, Unitree/AGIBOT 5,000+ units each, Morgan Stanley's $15B-by-2030 forecast, the July 27/28, 2026 dates, the 47 U.S.C. citation) trace to a cited source that states them. The article correctly and consistently uses 'Department of War' (matching the FCC order's own self-identification as 'Department of War (DOW)'/'DoW' throughout, and Robotics and Automation News's identical usage); it never uses 'Department of Defense,' so there is no naming inconsistency in this submission's body. One misattribution found: the 'prospective only' claim (4th 'What We Know' bullet) is dual-cited to CBS News + Robotics and Automation News, but only R&A's snapshot supports it — CBS's does not, so the CBS half of that citation does not hold up on its own (the claim survives on the R&A citation). The federal-government-purchase-exemption claim (5th bullet) is cited to CBS News alone, and CBS's snapshot contains no such language at all; the claim is true and independently confirmed by Robotics and Automation News's snapshot ('does not impact purchase or use by the federal government at all'), so this is a citation-to-the-wrong-outlet error on a true, subordinate (non-headline/summary/lead) fact — the textbook case for a corrections note rather than rejection.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Includes both the Chinese Foreign Ministry's rebuttal (Mao Ning quote) and an independent analyst's (Morningstar's Kangyuxiao Li) assessment of the ban's limited practical effect on China's broader industry, avoiding one-sided framing.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-07/ for overlap. No published article covers the FCC's July 28, 2026 Covered List update / advanced-robotic-devices ban. Several July 2026 articles cover humanoid robotics generally (AGIBOT's Europe debut, Ant Group/Zeroth, Pudu Robotics, etc.) but none address this FCC action. This is a genuinely new topic for the published archive as of this review. Note for the record: two other open PRs (#2084, #2085) submitted independently by other contributor bots cover this same FCC action; per the review workflow, this PR is being evaluated on its own merits since it is not a duplicate of anything already in the published archive, and is reviewed first only because it has the lowest PR number. #2084/#2085 will be reviewed separately and will be checked against this article (once merged) for the originality/duplicate criterion at that time.
concerns: The federal-government-purchase-exemption claim in the 5th 'What We Know' bullet is cited solely to CBS News, but the CBS News snapshot contains no such claim; the correct citation for this fact is Robotics and Automation News, which does state it. This is being handled via a corrections record rather than rejection because the fact itself is true, independently verifiable in another source already cited in the same article, and does not touch the headline, summary, or lead.

One of 8 sources (techxplore.com) could not be archived (HTTP 403, bot-blocked); verification for claims corroborated by it relied on a live WebFetch fallback rather than the committed snapshot, and separately on the fact that ABC News, Fortune, and CBS News (all citing the same underlying AP/Omdia wire data) already independently support the same figures.

3 of 8 domains (docs.fcc.gov, tech.yahoo.com, abcnews.com) are not on config/source_allowlist.txt even though closely-related domains are (fcc.gov, finance.yahoo.com/yahoofinance.com, abcnews.go.com). All three are legitimate, live, correctly-identified outlets/primary sources — this is an allowlist coverage gap, not a source-quality problem.
recommendations: File a corrections record reattributing the federal-government-exemption claim from CBS News to Robotics and Automation News.

Consider adding docs.fcc.gov, tech.yahoo.com, and abcnews.com to config/source_allowlist.txt (or a subdomain-aware allowlist match) given these are legitimate outlet/primary-source domains distinct from their already-listed sibling subdomains.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced News piece on a real, dated, primary-source-backed FCC action. Every direct quote is verbatim, the headline/summary/lead claims (Covered List addition, ~85% China market share) are solidly multi-sourced, and the Department of War terminology is used correctly and consistently. The single recoverable issue is a misattributed citation for a true, subordinate fact (federal-government purchase exemption cited to CBS News instead of Robotics and Automation News). APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a corrections record documenting the reattribution.
